title: TrustAnchor::from_cert silently drops malformed NameConstraints
description:
TrustAnchor::from_cert (line 706 in pkix-path/src/lib.rs) silently sets name_constraints = None when the anchor cert's NameConstraints extension has malformed DER. The doc comment explains this behavior and directs callers to TrustAnchor::try_from for strict handling. However, the fail-open semantics are a silent security gap: a deployment that intended 'this root may only sign for *.example.com' via NameConstraints would silently lose that constraint if the extension's DER is malformed.

The alternative constructor TrustAnchor::try_from exists and propagates the error, and pkix-truststore uses it (from_pem at line 524: 'TrustAnchor::try_from(c).map_err(Error::Der)'). So the strict path is available and used in the canonical trust-store loader.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Callers who construct TrustAnchor via from_cert (the consuming-ownership path, typical for manual anchor construction) get fail-open behavior on malformed NameConstraints. The constraint is silently dropped. The non-consuming From<&Certificate> impl at line 717 has the same fail-open behavior. Both are documented, but the default-and-easy path is fail-open while the strict path requires the caller to know to use try_from.

This is a defensive-code-forcing concern: the natural/easy constructor is the unsafe one. The safe constructor requires the caller to make a deliberate choice. The pkix-truststore crate already made the right choice, but nothing in the API surface steers callers toward try_from.

Locations:
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-path/src/lib.rs line 706 (from_cert)
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-path/src/lib.rs line 717 (From<&Certificate>)
